headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write/modify shared files and git state while Airflow can egress broadly, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Cline reads workspace files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; if Airflow outputs attacker-controlled content into shared files or APIs, Cline may ingest it as instructions. The pair has a shared filesystem bridge via Cline's workspace model, so interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF Airflow writes untrusted content into a workspace file that Cline later reads
IF Cline is configured to treat file contents or MCP payloads as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict Airflow outputs to non-executable formats
Separate Airflow and Cline workspaces
Disable MCP servers for the Cline session
Add provenance labels to files exchanged between agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline can read and write workspace files, capture browser screenshots, and send data to model providers/MCP servers; Airflow has broad network egress. If sensitive code or screenshots enter the shared workspace, Cline can transmit them outward, while Airflow can move data off-host. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace
IF Cline is connected to a third-party model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a separate least-privilege workspace for Cline
Disable browser screenshots when handling sensitive data
Rotate model-provider keys after any exposure
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state via filesystem; Airflow can also affect files through its automation outputs and broad egress. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking, making destructive overwrite or repository corruption plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or git repository
IF neither side uses external locking or coordination
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or directories
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Add a manual file-locking convention
requires-engineering: implement workspace locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can act on workspace content and git state, so if it treats Airflow-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or tool actions. Airflow's broad egress increases the chance that generated outputs are stale or externally sourced, and Cline's default automation makes downstream execution plausible.
conditions: IF Cline consumes Airflow-generated files or reports without verification
IF Cline is allowed to commit or execute actions based on those artifacts
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Add checksum or schema validation on Airflow outputs
Mark Airflow artifacts as untrusted inputs
Limit Cline to read-only mode for generated files
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so a compliance breach is not established. However, Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots while Airflow has broad egress, so compliance risk exists if regulated data is routed through the pair; Airflow is cited for egress and Cline for sensitive surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in the shared workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server lacks the required residency or retention controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace
Document the model provider's residency and retention settings
Disable screenshots for regulated workflows
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
